symptoms: HTTP 503 Service Unavailable
High P99 latency (>4500ms)
Database connection timeouts on checkout endpoints
error_logs: Timeout waiting for database connection from pool
Connection pool exhausted (active=50, max=50)
HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 30005ms
root_cause: Database connection pool exhaustion during a sudden flash-sale traffic spike due to default max_connections=50.
investigation_steps: Inspect active database connection count vs max pool size
Check RDS/Postgres CPU and IOPS utilization to ensure DB itself is healthy
Review checkout API traffic surge metrics (RPS jumped from 120 to 850 RPS)
Verify connection leak by monitoring idle-in-transaction connection holding times
resolution_steps: Increase database connection pool capacity from 50 to 150 in Payment API configuration
Deploy hotfix configuration change and trigger rolling restart of Payment API pods
Monitor 5xx error rate and pool saturation in Datadog
runbook: 1. Query pg_stat_activity to count open connections per client IP
2. Check Payment API /metrics endpoint for hikaricp_pending_threads
3. If pending > 0 and DB CPU < 40%, scale pool size via Helm values
4. Execute rolling restart with zero-downtime
5. Verify 503 errors drop below 0.01% within 2 minutes
lessons_learned: Traffic spikes can exhaust the configured connection pool before the database server reaches compute limits
Connection pool size must auto-scale or be dimensioned for 3x peak burst
Need circuit breaker on checkout service to degrade gracefully instead of hanging threads

symptoms: Session lookup latency spikes
Cache write failures with OOM command not allowed
Users unexpectedly logged out across multiple regions
error_logs: OOM command not allowed when used memory > 'maxmemory'
Redis write failed: command rejected due to memory limits (used_memory=16.1GB, maxmemory=16.0GB)
root_cause: Key TTLs were accidentally omitted on new user preference payloads, filling the 16GB Redis cluster without an eviction policy set to volatile-lru.
investigation_steps: Check redis-cli INFO memory used_memory_human vs maxmemory
Inspect eviction policy config: maxmemory-policy
Run redis-cli --bigkeys to identify runaway key patterns without TTL
resolution_steps: Switch eviction policy to allkeys-lru dynamically via CONFIG SET maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru
Run purge script on expired session prefixes
Patch preferences service to strictly enforce 24h TTL
runbook: 1. Verify memory: redis-cli info memory
2. Set policy: CONFIG SET maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru
3. Check eviction rate: redis-cli info stats | grep evicted_keys
4. Deploy TTL fix commit to preferences microservice
lessons_learned: All keys written to shared Redis clusters must have an explicit TTL
Eviction policy must never be noeviction on ephemeral session caches

symptoms: Orders stuck in PENDING queue
Worker pods failing to start
Kubelet reporting CrashLoopBackOff
error_logs: Back-off 5m0s restarting failed container: order-worker
Error: failed to parse YAML config: mapping values are not allowed here at line 42
Fatal error during startup: invalid configuration file syntax
root_cause: A malformed ConfigMap containing a tab character in YAML indentation was merged during the staging deployment.
investigation_steps: kubectl describe pod order-worker-7d9b4c-kx82z
kubectl logs order-worker-7d9b4c-kx82z --previous
kubectl get configmap order-worker-config -o yaml | yamllint -
resolution_steps: Correct indentation in order-worker-config ConfigMap
Re-apply ConfigMap via kubectl apply
Restart deployment order-worker with kubectl rollout restart
runbook: 1. Inspect pod events: kubectl describe pod -l app=order-worker
2. Check previous container exit code and logs
3. Validate ConfigMap syntax with linter
4. Roll back helm release or patch ConfigMap
5. Verify worker pods transition to Running state
lessons_learned: CI/CD pipeline must enforce strict yamllint and dry-run validation on all Kubernetes manifests prior to rollout
Never edit ConfigMaps directly in production without pipeline validation

symptoms: API Gateway returning 502 Bad Gateway to 100% of external traffic
Upstream services report healthy but unreachable through gateway
error_logs: [error] 142#0: *12049 name resolution failed for upstream service 'billing.internal': server failure (2: SERVFAIL)
502 Bad Gateway while connecting to upstream billing.internal:8080
root_cause: CoreDNS pods crashed due to memory exhaustion during a cluster node migration, leaving internal service discovery non-functional.
investigation_steps: Check Gateway error logs for upstream resolution errors
Verify CoreDNS pod status with kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l k8s-app=kube-dns
Test DNS lookup from within a debug pod using nslookup billing.internal
resolution_steps: Scale CoreDNS deployment to 4 replicas and increase memory limit to 256Mi
Restart Gateway worker processes to clear stale DNS resolver cache
Verify DNS resolution and monitor 502 error clearance
runbook: 1. Check DNS pods: kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l k8s-app=kube-dns
2. Inspect CoreDNS memory: kubectl -n kube-system top pods
3. If OOMKilled, patch memory request/limit to 256Mi
4. Flush Gateway resolver cache: nginx -s reload or pod restart
5. Verify HTTP 200 responses on external gateway ping endpoint
lessons_learned: CoreDNS is a single-point-of-failure for internal routing and must have node anti-affinity and adequate memory headroom
Gateway should cache DNS resolutions with resilient fallback TTL

symptoms: CPU utilization at 98% across all auth nodes
Auth response latency exceeding 3000ms
Downstream services timing out on token validation
error_logs: Thread starvation detected: 64 worker threads waiting on lock for RSA key cache
Slow request warning: Token validation took 4120ms
root_cause: Synchronized block around RSA public key decoding caused global thread contention under 500+ concurrent requests.
investigation_steps: Collect Java thread dump using jstack <pid>
Inspect top thread states: 48 threads BLOCKED on java.security.spec.X509EncodedKeySpec
Review recent git commits to AuthTokenValidator.java
resolution_steps: Replace synchronized key parsing block with pre-computed ConcurrentHashMap cache of PublicKey instances
Deploy hotfix release v2.4.1
Verify CPU utilization drops back below 25%
runbook: 1. Capture thread dump: jcmd <pid> Thread.dump_to_file /tmp/threads.tdump
2. Analyze lock contention with thread analyzer or grep for BLOCKED
3. Scale auth deployment temporarily to absorb traffic
4. Deploy non-blocking key cache patch
5. Monitor CPU and P95 latency
lessons_learned: Cryptographic key parsing is CPU intensive and should be parsed once on boot, never per request
Load test cryptographic verification paths under high concurrency

symptoms: Search queries failing with disk I/O errors
Elasticsearch nodes dropping into READ_ONLY mode
Node disk utilization reached 100%
error_logs: java.io.IOException: No space left on device
cluster_block_exception: index read-only / allow delete block active
root_cause: Logrotate daemon failed due to permissions error, allowing debug log files to balloon to 180GB.
investigation_steps: Check disk usage: df -h
Find largest files: find /var/log -type f -size +1G
Check logrotate systemd service status: systemctl status logrotate
resolution_steps: Truncate unrotated .log files: > /var/log/elasticsearch/debug.log
Fix file permissions in /etc/logrotate.d/elasticsearch
Remove cluster read-only block: curl -X PUT 'localhost:9200/_all/_settings' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"index.blocks.read_only_allow_delete": null}'
runbook: 1. Run df -h /var/log to verify saturation
2. Safely truncate largest log file without restarting process
3. Clear Elasticsearch floodstage block via REST API
4. Test logrotate with logrotate -f /etc/logrotate.d/elasticsearch
5. Set up alert at 80% disk threshold
lessons_learned: Log rotation must be actively monitored with alerting on logrotate failure
Disk watermarks must trigger alert at 80% well before 95% floodstage

symptoms: Users unable to sign in with Google/GitHub SSO
HTTP 429 Too Many Requests returned from OAuth callback
Login success rate dropped to 12%
error_logs: OAuth provider returned 429: Rate limit exceeded for client_id
Failed token exchange: rate limit reset in 320 seconds
root_cause: A frontend retry loop on network glitch caused 50,000 rapid token exchange requests, blowing the OAuth quota.
investigation_steps: Inspect outbound HTTP traffic metrics to oauth provider endpoints
Review frontend client telemetry for retry loops on button click
Verify provider quota dashboard
resolution_steps: Disable aggressive frontend retry and implement exponential backoff with jitter
Implement backend token exchange rate limiter and cache validated tokens
Request temporary quota increase from OAuth provider
runbook: 1. Verify 429 errors in identity proxy logs
2. Check frontend client version distribution for retry bug
3. Enable IP rate-limiting at Cloudflare edge to throttle rapid retries
4. Deploy frontend patch with disabled auto-retry
5. Monitor successful logins
lessons_learned: Frontend network retry logic must always use exponential backoff and never retry on 4xx status codes
OAuth token exchanges should be queued or debounced per user

symptoms: Notification delivery delayed by >45 minutes
Kafka consumer lag exceeding 1.2M messages
Consumer group repeatedly dropping members
error_logs: CommitFailedException: Commit cannot be completed since the group has already rebalanced
Heartbeat failed for group notification-workers: member timed out after max.poll.interval.ms
root_cause: A batch email template rendering job took 6 minutes, exceeding max.poll.interval.ms (5 minutes), triggering continuous consumer group rebalances.
investigation_steps: Check kafka-consumer-groups --describe --group notification-workers
Inspect consumer logs for CommitFailedException and rebalance events
Profile email rendering duration in APM traces
resolution_steps: Increase max.poll.interval.ms from 300,000ms to 900,000ms
Reduce max.poll.records from 500 to 50
Offload heavy HTML email rendering to an asynchronous threadpool
runbook: 1. Inspect consumer lag: kafka-consumer-groups.sh --bootstrap-server kafka:9092 --describe --group notification-workers
2. Check average batch processing time in Datadog
3. Update consumer config: max.poll.records=50, max.poll.interval.ms=900000
4. Restart consumer service instances gracefully
5. Verify lag steadily decreases to zero
lessons_learned: Long-running message processing must never block the Kafka consumer polling thread
Keep max.poll.records low when processing times are variable

symptoms: Invoice generation throwing HTTP 500 Internal Server Error
Customers unable to view invoices or download receipts
Error rate jumped to 45% immediately following deployment v3.8.0
error_logs: ProgrammingError: column invoices.tax_breakdown does not exist
SQLAlchemy OperationalError: (psycopg2.errors.UndefinedColumn) column "tax_breakdown" does not exist
root_cause: The v3.8.0 application deployment was promoted to production before the corresponding Alembic database migration had executed.
investigation_steps: Review deployment pipeline logs for 'alembic upgrade head' step
Query alembic_version table in PostgreSQL
Compare Git release tag v3.8.0 migration scripts with DB schema
resolution_steps: Run pending database migration: alembic upgrade head
Verify column tax_breakdown exists on invoices table
Confirm 500 error rate drops to 0%
runbook: 1. Inspect Sentry/logs for database schema errors
2. Check current migration revision: alembic current
3. Run migration in staging first, then apply to production: alembic upgrade head
4. Verify schema with \d+ invoices in psql
5. Test invoice creation endpoint with health test curl
lessons_learned: Database migrations must be decoupled and executed in an automated pre-deploy Kubernetes Job before app pods are updated
Deployments must fail fast if pending schema migrations are unapplied

symptoms: Item deletion API timing out after 60s
Postgres lock manager experiencing high lock waits
Catalog updates hanging
error_logs: Canceling statement due to statement timeout (60000ms)
Lock wait timeout exceeded while executing DELETE FROM categories WHERE id = $1
root_cause: The foreign key column product_items.category_id lacked an index, causing PostgreSQL to execute a full sequential table scan of 12M rows during cascading delete locks.
investigation_steps: Check pg_stat_activity for blocked queries and waiting PID
Run EXPLAIN ANALYZE on SELECT * FROM product_items WHERE category_id = 4501
Inspect pg_locks to identify exclusive table lock contention
resolution_steps: Execute CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_product_items_category_id ON product_items(category_id)
Cancel long-running stuck backend queries: SELECT pg_cancel_backend(pid)
Verify item deletion completes in under 40ms
runbook: 1. Query stuck locks: SELECT pid, query, state, age(clock_timestamp(), query_start) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state != 'idle'
2. Terminate blocking backend PID if safe
3. Create missing index CONCURRENTLY to avoid locking production table
4. Verify index status in pg_stat_user_indexes
5. Test deletion endpoint response time
lessons_learned: Always create explicit indexes on all foreign key columns referenced in ON DELETE CASCADE relations
Enable query performance insights and statement timeout alerts
